A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPoT study. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original ImageNet classification, kNN, oracle-placement, cross-model transfer and robustness results.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, with additional retrofitting convergence results and qualitative analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The bilinear subpixel tokenizer, positional embeddings, six spatial priors and frozen-encoder SPoT-ON search are retained. Added retrofitting explanations do not establish an implemented methodological change; the policy network discussed in Section 7 remains future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet training and classification coverage. The additional comparisons and analyses remain within that coverage; detection and video applications are proposed only as future directions.

E2.justification: New Table 8 adds ToMe as a reported comparator using its published results, including inference-time reduction and a fine-tuned MAE variant. ToMe was previously only cited. Existing ViT and ElasticViT comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added ToMe comparison selects 100-token SPoT configurations and ToMe configurations with the highest reported speed-up, measuring changes relative to full-token baselines. Appendix D also reports behavior at 20 or more oracle iterations. Existing main settings remain listed unchanged, although Section 5.2's new i.i.d. uniform sampling description conflicts with the retained isotropic sampler in Table 7, leaving any actual sampler change unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds training and validation curves supporting the 50-epoch retrofitting duration. Appendix D adds saliency-overlaid trajectories across priors, adversarial trajectory examples and an iteration-related boundary failure observation. These extend existing analyses; the 30-image descent panel moved from v1's appendix to v2's Figure 4 is retained evidence.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same uncertainty entries for stochastic-prior kNN results. No new seed counts, repeated-run specifications, confidence intervals or statistical tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–6 and the ElasticViT comparison are unchanged. New Table 8 reports, for example, CLS-IN21k speed-up/accuracy-drop pairs of 3.31×/−2.95 for SPoT and 1.95×/−4.20 for ToMe under the selected configurations. New findings include retrofitting convergence and placements leaving image boundaries after extended oracle optimization. Table C.1 supplies exact throughput values accompanying the existing Figure 5 analysis.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds an arithmetic-cost derivation, T·k²·(7C+8) FLOPs, and an asymptotic comparison with transformer computation. The original six numbered equations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain continuous token placement, oracle analysis of sparse placements and investigation of spatial priors. The introduction now foregrounds SPoT-ON as an analysis tool providing an empirical performance bound, a qualification already present in v1's Section 3.2.

C2.justification: The conclusion develops possible learned placement policies and task-dependent extensions to detection and video. Appendix D adds the warning that visually plausible or randomly sampled placements can harm performance. These extend applicability and failure discussions without changing the principal interpretations of existing results.

D1.justification: Appendix A clarifies trainable parameters, retained training objectives and joint encoder/head fine-tuning. Appendix B specifies the validation preprocessing used for its convergence curve, and acknowledgments disclose access to LUMI. Existing hyperparameter tables and the code-access link are retained; v1's evaluation-protocol appendix is relocated to Section 5.2.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged, but Section 6 expands positioning against ToMe by explaining progressive token merging versus SPoT's initial token sampling and constant subsequent token count. This is a limited substantive extension of the prior-work comparison.

P1.justification: Most main prose and section order are retained. Local revisions clarify oracle terminology and retrofitting, expand the conclusion, relocate the evaluation protocol and reorganize the appendices. Citations change from numerical to author–year style.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout with substantial resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 4 incorporates v1's 30-image appendix panel; new convergence and qualitative figures and ToMe/throughput tables are added. Table 1 gains an explicit Oracle column.

improvement.justification: The ToMe comparison, retrofitting convergence evidence, computational-cost derivation and additional failure analysis provide useful support and transparency beyond v1 while preserving its core results. The gain is limited by a new reproducibility ambiguity: Section 5.2 describes i.i.d. uniform training positions while Table 7 still specifies isotropic sampling. Overall, the additional evidence supports a modest quality improvement.
